To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nature of dynamical processes in social networks should be taken into account when measuring centrality, and that non-conservative measures of centrality, such as Alpha-Centrality, are more suitable for ranking users in online networks used for broadcasting than conservative measures, such as PageRank.

(i) non-conservative processes are more suitable for modeling social dynamics, (ii) non-conservative Alpha-centrality is more accurate than conservative PageRank in ranking users in social networks used for information broadcasting, and (iii) our findings are supported by empirical results from two large-scale online social networks.
